_comment_family: Garet ships as a family, and the file in fonts/ is the Book weight of
it. Unlike the two Telegraf packs or the two Open Sans ones, this is
the only cut of the family the app carries, so there is no sibling
here for a bare family name to be confused with.
It is declared as 'Garet Book' all the same, which is name ID 1 of
this file rather than a full name invented for it: the file's own
typographic family (ID 16) is 'Garet' with 'Book' as the subfamily,
and ID 1 has already been split the way every pack here splits it by
hand. Declaring what the file says is both the honest answer and the
one that keeps working the day a second cut is added — an UltraBold
dropped in beside this one would carry its own ID 1 and could not
Weight 300, which is what the file's OS/2 table says. Book is a shade
lighter than a regular and that is the point of the cut; asking for
400 here would invite a browser to synthesise a weight the file does
_comment_css: Not declared in styles.css: this face arrived with a channel and is
registered from this JSON, which is the route content/README.md
describes. Nothing has to be added to the stylesheet for it.
_comment_local: What the machine may already know the face by, tried after the file.
The first is the PostScript name and is also what the installer
registers the face under; the second is the Windows full name. Both
name this one cut rather than the family, so a machine answering to
either is answering with this file — which is exactly what the
fallback route is for. 'Garet' on its own is deliberately absent: it
is the typographic family, and every other weight of Garet answers to
_comment_stack: The fallbacks are damage limitation and never a design choice — a
title laid out against the wrong metrics is broken, not merely
different, which is what fontguard exists to catch before it is ever
drawn. They are still chosen rather than copied: Garet is a geometric
sans built on circles, so the nearest thing a Windows machine can be
relied on to have is Century Gothic, and Segoe UI stands behind it
for the machine that somehow lacks even that. Impact and Arial Black
are absent for telegraf-ultralight's reason — they are heavy display
cuts, and putting one behind a 300-weight geometric would make the
one thing that survives a missing file the furthest possible thing
